kf: **IgA vasculitis** (Henoch–Schönlein purpura) is the commonest childhood vasculitis: **palpable purpura** on the buttocks and legs.
Tetrad: purpura, arthralgia/arthritis, abdominal pain (intussusception risk) and **renal involvement** (haematuria, proteinuria).
Often follows an upper respiratory infection; ages 3–10.
First exclude **meningococcal sepsis** in an unwell child with a non-blanching rash.
Supportive care; monitor **urine and BP** for 6–12 months; adults have more renal disease.

sub: About 20 per 100,000 children per year; autumn and winter; adults less often but more severely.

myths: **"The rash settled, so follow-up can stop"**: nephritis can appear weeks to months later.
patho_lead: Abnormal **IgA1** forms immune complexes that lodge in small vessels.

mech.t: Galactose-deficient IgA1 is produced after a mucosal infection.
IgA complexes deposit in small vessel walls in skin, gut, joints and kidney.
Neutrophils damage vessels and red cells leak: palpable purpura.
mech.cap: Small-vessel vasculitis: immune complexes on the vessel wall attract neutrophils that fragment and damage it, letting red cells leak out (palpable purpura).

mech.t: Mesangial IgA deposits cause haematuria and proteinuria.

histo: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA on direct IF of a new lesion.
comp: Nephritis and chronic kidney disease, intussusception, orchitis.
prog: Most children recover in 4–6 weeks; recurrence in a third.
